result.title: Understanding the Effect of Visual Attention in CNNs: A Decision-Space Alignment Perspective
result.summary: Visual Attention enhances convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by modulating intermediate features, yet their effects on downstream decisions remain less understood. We present a decision-space framework that models multiplicative attention as an intermediate feature perturbation and derives a first-order prediction of its effect on the target-versus-competitor classification margin. We further introduce the Decision Alignment Score (DAS) to quantify the directional alignment between the perturbation and the local margin gradient. We evaluate the framework on CIFAR-100 using SimAM and CBAM across five popular CNN backbones, ResNet-18, ResNet-20, ResNet-50, ResNet-56, and MobileNetV2. The analysis examines prediction agreement, DAS margin correlations, and downstream activation-state changes. Across most final-attention configurations, predicted and actual margin changes show good agreement, while DAS exhibits positive correlations with actual margin changes. Single-attention experiments further show that prediction agreement and DAS margin correlations depend on attention placement, with stronger associations at later stages.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出决策空间框架，把 CNN 中的乘性视觉注意力视为中间特征扰动，用一阶近似预测其对目标-竞争者分类间隔的影响，并引入 Decision Alignment Score 衡量扰动方向与局部 margin 梯度的对齐程度，在 CIFAR-100 上用 SimAM、CBAM 与五种 CNN 骨干做了验证，发现注意力位置越靠后预测一致性越强。
AI.relevance_reason: 该一阶扰动-间隔预测与方向对齐打分可能可供核查为「视觉证据对最终决策贡献」的定量归因工具，用于检验 VLM 中视觉注意或视觉 token 调制是否真正进入 latent 推理状态，但论文限于 CNN 分类，尚无多模态或 latent 推理证据。
